claims.claim: For a latency-sensitive idempotent read, the resilience guide says to consider hedging after measurement.
claims.actor: Implementer choosing resilience for outbound reads
claims.trigger: latency-sensitive idempotent read when consulting the private resilience decision guide
claims.exceptions: Consideration after measurement, not mandatory hedging; duplicate execution must be safe and ordinary need/lifetime constraints remain. No runtime measurement or API behavior observed.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Table called duplicate; safe hedging and general measurement preference or demonstrated optimization need do not unambiguously require measurement before considering hedging.
Preferring measurement for non-trivial optimizations may cover the table intent, but exact after-measurement timing is not expressed.
Hedging restrictions and provider/publication handling are captured; unclear whether the broad hedging record imports the timing qualifier.

claims.comparison_reason: Same-location table is a possible stronger temporal condition than general evidence preference; normativity and semantic subsumption remain open.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: A safe idempotent read has an unmeasured, reasoned latency concern; the implementer considers hedging before collecting measurements. General need and duplicate-safety constraints may hold while the literal ordering differs.
claims.open_question: Does after measurement independently constrain consideration, or summarize the already-registered general measured-optimization guidance?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Family5 compare temporal/modality implications; family6 root performance rule versus private-reference table. No mandatory adoption or proven EXTRA conclusion.
